title: execessive memory use with GnuTLS
body:
I'm running s3fs, built on libcurl.  By default this creates a pool of 20 `curl_easy_init` handles and reuses them with a `curl_easy_reset` between each `curl_easy_perform`.  `curl_easy_cleanup` is called when the pool is destroyed.

After a while the memory usage grows hugely.  Valgrind massif logging shows 100MB of ASN data:

```
 89.99% (286,590,012B) (heap allocation functions) malloc/new/new[], --alloc-fns, etc.
->34.88% (111,074,304B) 0x94E5122: ??? (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libtasn1.so.6.5.5)
| ->24.97% (79,520,320B) 0x94E249F: ??? (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libtasn1.so.6.5.5)
| | ->12.85% (40,930,560B) 0x94E1A7A: asn1_der_decoding2 (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libtasn1.so.6.5.5)
| | | ->12.85% (40,930,560B) 0x747818A: gnutls_x509_crt_import (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgnutls.so.30.14.10)
| | | | ->12.85% (40,930,560B) 0x747C4A3: gnutls_x509_crt_list_import (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgnutls.so.30.14.10)
| | | | | ->12.85% (40,930,560B) 0x747C786: gnutls_x509_crt_list_import2 (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgnutls.so.30.14.10)
| | | | |   ->12.85% (40,930,560B) 0x74852F0: gnutls_x509_trust_list_add_trust_mem (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgnutls.so.30.14.10)
| | | | |     ->12.85% (40,930,560B) 0x74857B5: gnutls_x509_trust_list_add_trust_file (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgnutls.so.30.14.10)
| | | | |       ->09.65% (30,717,984B) 0x7485A7B: ??? (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgnutls.so.30.14.10)
| | | | |       | ->09.65% (30,717,984B) 0x7485AC9: gnutls_x509_trust_list_add_trust_dir (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgnutls.so.30.14.10)
| | | | |       |   ->09.65% (30,717,984B) 0x74254F8: gnutls_certificate_set_x509_trust_dir (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgnutls.so.30.14.10)
| | | | |       |     ->09.65% (30,717,984B) 0x50CC456: ??? (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcurl-gnutls.so.4.5.0)
| | | | |       |       ->09.65% (30,717,984B) 0x50CE148: ??? (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcurl-gnutls.so.4.5.0)
| | | | |       |         ->09.65% (30,717,984B) 0x50807F0: ??? (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcurl-gnutls.so.4.5.0)
| | | | |       |           ->09.65% (30,717,984B) 0x508D124: ??? (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcurl-gnutls.so.4.5.0)
| | | | |       |             ->09.65% (30,717,984B) 0x50A2AB4: ??? (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcurl-gnutls.so.4.5.0)
| | | | |       |               ->09.65% (30,717,984B) 0x50A3A31: curl_multi_perform (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcurl-gnutls.so.4.5.0)
| | | | |       |                 ->09.65% (30,717,984B) 0x5099A12: curl_easy_perform (in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcurl-gnutls.so.4.5.0)
:
```

It looks like `gnutls_certificate_set_x509_trust_dir` might be *adding* certificates on every call to `curl_easy_perform`?

Should `gnutls_certificate_free_credentials` be being called in `curl_easy_reset` (as it is in `curl_easy_cleanup`)?  Or should the call to `gnutls_certificate_set_x509_trust_dir` be being made in `curl_easy_init` maybe?

### curl/libcurl version

curl 7.58.0 (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu) libcurl/7.58.0 OpenSSL/1.1.1 zlib/1.2.11 libidn2/2.0.4 libpsl/0.19.1 (+libidn2/2.0.4) nghttp2/1.30.0 librtmp/2.3
